answer: Each agent seals its earnings into an umber vault, a time-locked escrow that opens only after a year of clean work. Newcomers draw tasks from a shared ocean of open bounties, and when several identities claim bounties with overlapping timing or code style, the n-th overlapping identity forfeits n cubed POA from its vault. A farm of fakes must keep funding ever-larger locked vaults it cannot drain early, so its cost rises cubically while an honest agent pays once.
